paper.title: Offline Neural Contextual Bandits: Pessimism, Optimization and Generalization

settings.name_in_paper: Offline stochastic K-armed contextual bandit with neural network function approximation
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline policy learning from a fixed logged dataset (no interaction); not an interactive bandit problem.
unmapped: Offline setting: learner only has n logged samples collected by an unknown (possibly adaptive, non-stationary) behaviour policy mu
Unknown reward function h: R^d -> [0,1] with R-subgaussian conditional noise; no functional form assumed
NTK Gram matrix H >= lambda_0 I on observed contexts; the learner's tuning uses lambda_0 (network width and beta_t depend on it)
Context vectors on the unit sphere with duplicated-coordinate structure
settings.definition_quote: In the offline contextual bandit setting, the goal is to learn an optimal policy only from an offline data $\mathcal{D}_n = \{ (\bm{x}_t,a_t, r_t) \}_{t=1}^n$ collected a priori by a behaviour policy $\mu$. ... For each $t$, $r_t = h( \bm{x}_{t, a_t}) + \xi_t$, where $h: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow [0,1]$ is an unknown reward function, and $\xi_t$ is a $R$-subgaussian noise conditioned on $(\mathcal{D}_{t-1}, \bm{x}_t, a_t)$

symbols.d_eff: effective dimension of the NTK matrix, log det(I+H/lambda)/log(1+nK/lambda)

conditions: Assumption 4.1: NTK matrix H >= lambda_0 I, ||x^(i)||_2 = 1, duplicated-coordinate structure of inputs
Assumption 4.2: contexts x_t independent of D_{t-1}; ||pi*(.|x_t)/mu(.|D_{t-1},x_t)||_inf <= kappa
h maps into [0,1], noise R-subgaussian conditionally on the past
tuning: beta_t = sqrt(lambda + C_3^2 t L)(t^{1/2} lambda^{-1/2} + (nK)^{1/2} lambda_0^{-1/2}) m^{-1/2}
eta_t = iota/sqrt(t), iota^{-1} = Omega(n^{2/3} m^{5/6} lambda^{-1/6} L^{17/6} log^{1/2} m) v Omega(m lambda^{1/2} log^{1/2}(nKL^2(10n+4)/delta))

source.label: main_theorem
source.quote: For any $\delta \in (0,1)$, under Assumption \ref{assumption:ntk_input_data} and \ref{assumption:distributional_shift}, if the network width $m$, ... then with probability at least $1 - \delta$ over the randomness of $\bm{W}^{(0)}$ and $\mathcal{D}_n$, the sub-optimality of $\hat{\pi}$ returned by Algorithm 1 is bounded as $n \cdot \mathbb{E} [\subopt(\hat{\pi}) ] \leq  \kappa \sqrt{n}  \sqrt{\tilde{d} \log(1 + nK/\lambda)  + 2} +  \kappa \sqrt{n}  + 2 + \sqrt{2 n \log((10n+4)/\delta)}$

results.notes: Theorem bounds n*E[SubOpt]; expression divided by n to give the expected sub-optimality of the returned (randomly selected) policy, measured against the per-context optimal policy over the context distribution. Expectation is over the uniform choice of hat-pi; overall statement is w.p. 1-delta over initialization and data. Paper simplifies to O~(kappa max{sqrt(d_tilde),1} n^{-1/2}). Offline setting, out of scope.
